fact.thing: tax refunded on a $10,000 capital loss carried back
fact.box: Taxable (non-registered) account, past 3 years' returns via Form T1A
fact.claim: You can use a net capital loss to cut your taxable capital gains in any of the three previous years, or carry it forward with no time limit. To carry it back you file Form T1A, and you don't amend the old return. Half of the loss counts (the 50% inclusion rate), and it can only offset capital gains, not wages or other income. For an Ontario resident earning just over $58,523, that half is taxed at a combined 29.65%, so a $10,000 loss gets back about $1,483 of tax paid on earlier gains. This is an example: the real refund depends on your tax rate in the year the gain was taxed.

plain.what: If you lost money on bitcoin, that loss does not have to sit in the year it happened. Bitcoin is a digital coin people trade online. The CRA, Canada's tax office, lets you send a net capital loss backward to an earlier year, using Form T1A, Part 5, filed with this year's return.
plain.so_what: A 2025 loss can reach back 3 years, to 2022, 2023 or 2024, so it can cut gains you already paid tax on. But it only cuts capital gains, not your job income.
plain.do: Open your last 3 tax returns today and write down whether any of them show a capital gain.
